## What it is

The drip tray of the scale, in the Profitec GO's base plate. A watertight PETG tub, one solid, modelled in the machine frame (X from the base plate's left inner wall, Y from the machine face toward the user, Z from the top of the base plate floor) and returned through `scale_frame`. It takes the plate's full inner width in front of the machine face, narrows to the mouth's width behind it, runs 23 mm into the mouth and hangs from the plate's side walls by two narrow flanges. One flat floor, underside at Z 20, over the whole tray; the rear is a 45° slope over the full width: the purge water falls on it and runs forward. A Ø42 round window with a round kerb lets the tower through to the load cell; the TPU chimney (`scale_chimney`) pushes over the kerb. Rails along both side walls carry the outer grille with the front wall top. Two pegs grow out of the slope toward the mouth: the west one meets the machine's bumper, the east one carries the TPU `scale_bumper`. It prints floor on the bed, in the pose it has in the machine. Bambu PETG Basic, printed on the P2S.

## Design notes

Every mating dimension comes from `scale_layout().tray`; the base plate and mouth from `measurements.toml`. Body X 0.5 to 192.5 from Y 7 to 139.5 (the plate's 193 less 0.5 per wall), X 9.5 to 183.5 (the mouth) from Y -23 to 7, walls and floor 2.5 (the cavity is the outer section offset inward by one wall, so floor and wall must be equal: `reject` otherwise).

- Floor: underside at 20.0 everywhere, top at 22.5. It must stay 1.3 mm (`SCALE_CLEARANCE`) over the highest part of the scale under it (`_scale_tops`): the base's bridge beam 18.7, the adapter 18.7, the PCB box lid 18.6. Going lower means thinning the beam and the adapter together (the adapter's 3 mm over the cell is set by its magnet wells), then the lid.
- **Full width in front of the machine face.** From `wide_y0` (Y 7) forward the side walls stand 0.5 inside the plate's walls (X 0.5 to 3.0, 190.0 to 192.5): they locate the tray in X. Y 7 clears by 1 mm the two screw heads in the machine face at the plate's top corners (out to Y 6, axis at Z 29, `scale_vis_facade_*`); behind it the tray keeps the mouth's width. Above Z 31.5 a 45° shoulder leans 9 mm inward from each wall and meets the rail's corbel in one line at X 12 / Z 40.5, so the outer grille keeps its width (168.4, A1 mini). Over the shoulder the part is solid up to the rim (48.5), flush with the outer grille's top.
- **No front lock.** The floor is 3 mm above the base plate's front lip (17): the tray slides straight in over it and nothing holds it forward any more (`reject` if the underside comes within 1 mm of the lip). Side play is 0.5 per side; toward the machine, the pegs stop 1 mm from the bumpers. Toward the user, the tray is free until the outer grille's cut-out touches the cup grille (2 mm) or the kerb touches the tower (3 mm); either contact shunts the weight. Indexing it is an open choice (owner, 2026-11-17).
- Rear slope: one 45° plane over the whole width, 2.5 thick measured square to it; its inner face reaches the rim (48.5) at Y -23 and meets the floor's top at Y 3.0. Its underside meets the floor's underside at Y 2.0; behind that the tray is 18 mm or more above the rear lip (12) and the screw heads.
- Window and kerb: circles on the tower axis (97, 54). Window Ø42 through the floor and the kerb; kerb 2 thick, from the floor (22.5) to 35.5. The chimney's 1.6 sleeve over it reaches a radius of 24.6, on the flat floor (`reject` if it reaches the slope or the side walls).
- Front wall: Y 137 to 139.5, from the floor up to the rails' level, 46.0. The outer grille bears on the full 2.5 of its top: 421 mm².
- Rails: 3.0 wide, 2.5 thick, top at 46.0, along both side walls only, on a 45° corbel down to 40.5. They run from the front wall back to where the rear slope cuts them (Y -20.5 at their top). Contact with the outer grille: 424 mm² each.
- Shoulders: 2 mm flange, Z 47 to 49, Y 7 to 139.5, from the side walls' outer face (X 0.5) to the plate walls' outer face (X -2.0 / 195.0): 2.5 mm over the wall top and its play, nothing beyond. The load on them is negligible: about 0.8 kg (tray, water, outer grille) over 2 x 132 mm of flange, under 0.1 MPa at the root. The flange's top stands 0.5 above the rim (48.5), too little for a 1 mm chamfer, so that edge stays sharp.
- Rear pegs, Ø10 along -Y, solid where they cross the slope (the part that would reach into the tub is cut away with the cavity). West at (49.5, Z 32), end at Y -23: 1 mm in front of the machine's bumper tip (-24). East at (157.5, Z 32), end at Y -29.5, for the TPU cap (end of cap at -31, 1 mm from the back of the mouth). Each has a 2.5 structural 45° fill at the root.
- Water, computed from the model up to Z 43.5 (the rails' underside), minus the rails and the kerb's column (the window inside it is sealed by the chimney): 508 cm³ (0.51 L), 388 up to Z 38.5; the chimney's sleeve takes about 5 cm³ more. The full-width part adds 31 cm³ over a tray at the mouth's width. The tray with a front well held 649; version 1 held 0.69 L to 5 mm below its brim.
- Part volume 150 cm³ (unpolished), about 190 g of PETG at 100 % fill; the slicer's infill takes most of the solid over the shoulders.
- Guards (`reject`, from the layout): full-width part on the machine face's screw heads, floor and wall unequal, rim more than 49.0 (mouth ceiling 51 minus 2), floor underside under 20.0 (highest part of the scale under it plus 1.3) or within 1 mm of the front lip, body wider than the mouth, rear end past the left bumper (Y -24), chimney sleeve off the flat floor.
- Polish: 1 mm on straight convex edges, skipping the faces other parts bear on (shoulder undersides, locating faces, rail and front wall tops, the side walls' inner top edges that guide the grille in), the kerb and window, every edge in the floor's underside (the bed), every edge whose chamfer would face more than 45° downward, and acute edges (the rear rim, where a chamfer leaves a sliver thinner than the knife it blunts).

### Printing

Floor on the bed, as modelled: 197 x 169 x 29 mm on the P2S's 256 mm bed. First layer 24 929 mm², the whole floor: print with a brim (`warp_risk`). The window is a vertical round hole, the kerb a plain ring, the rear slope's underside exactly 45°.

`nurb check` lists what needs support, all of it expected:

- The shoulders: each flange stands 2.5 mm out from the side wall at Z 47, 132 mm long: 330 mm² per side at 90°, and its ends read as floating. A 2.5 mm ledge prints as an overhang without support on the P2S; accepted (owner, 2026-11-17).
- The two rear pegs: horizontal Ø10 cylinders under the rear slope, 7 to 17 mm over the bed, and their root fills (69°). Supports from the bed.

## Don't

- Do not put back a front well or a lower zone: the tray prints floor on the bed only while the floor is one plane.
- Do not go back to a lens-shaped window: it existed to print standing on the front wall; flat, the round hole prints as it is.
- Do not chamfer the shoulder undersides, the locating faces, the rail tops or the front wall top, nor add a lead-in on the inner top edges of the walls; do not chamfer the kerb, the window or the pegs.
- Do not chamfer the rear rim's edge, nor any acute edge: the 1 mm chamfer left a 0.21 mm section.
- Do not raise the pegs' root fill to 3 mm: on the east peg it did not land.
- Do not open the slope behind the pegs: it holds water.
- Do not bring the full-width part behind Y 7: the screw heads in the machine face stand out to Y 6. There are no screws on the side walls themselves (owner, 2026-11-17).
- Do not put back locating corbels or wide wings: the full-width side walls locate the tray, and the flanges only cover the wall tops.
- Do not widen the rails to the full-width walls: the outer grille would grow to about 186 mm, past the A1 mini's bed.
- Do not put anything on the floor around the kerb: the chimney's sleeve stands there.
- Do not put back the splash ball: the rear slope catches the purge water now and turns it forward.
- Do not print it standing on its front wall again, nor tilted: that print pose is what forced the well, the ramps and the lens; tilted, it stood 143 mm tall on an 8 mm facet.

## Changelog

- 2026-11-16 — First model, upright in the machine frame: raised zone and full-width well behind a vertical well wall, rails on three sides, shoulders, window and kerb, splash ball, peg on a vertical rear wall. It needed supports to print.
- 2026-11-16 — Tilted print: a `diagonal` variant stood at 45° on an 8 mm facet cut across the front-bottom edge, shoulders cut at 45° in plan, rear rail without corbel. Dropped: 143 mm tall on 8 mm of adhesion, and the facet ate into the well's corner.
- 2026-11-16 — Rebuilt to print standing on the front wall (`standing` variant; the default stays in the frame for the assembly): plateau with a 45° ramp beside a gently sloping west zone and a divider wall; 45° rear slope instead of a rear wall; lens-shaped window and kerb on the plateau's flat; side rails only; square front wall top (no bevel); square shoulder ends; corbels from the front to Y 40; both pegs on the slope with a root fill; splash ball, rear rail, well wall, `diagonal` and `stand_facet` removed.
- 2026-11-16 - Web under the kerb's +Y tip; the standing variant checks clean.
- 2026-11-17 - Plateau underside 25 -> 20, the floor set by the scale under it (beam and adapter at 18.7, plus 1.3): 5 mm more water over the plateau. The guard now checks the beam, the adapter and the lid, not the adapter alone. Kerb 8 -> 13 mm tall over the floor.
- 2026-11-17 - Flat floor: underside at Z 20 over the whole tray, printed floor on the bed. Front well, west zone, divider, ramps, kerb web and the `standing` variant removed; window and kerb round (`scale_circle`, Ø42). The tray no longer locks behind the front lip. Capacity 649 -> 477 cm³.
- 2026-11-17 - Full width in front of the machine face (X 0.5 to 192.5 from Y 7), 45° shoulders 9 mm inward to the unchanged rails, flanges cut to the wall tops (2.5 mm), locating corbels removed. Capacity 477 -> 508 cm³.
